title.narrative: Joint Executive Program for the Malaria Control and Prevention Project in Yemen, Phase II

description.narrative: The overall objective of the project is: 1- Providing basic diagnostic tools for malaria and arthropod-borne viral diseases. 2- Reactivation of quality assurance and quality control for malaria control in 100 health facilities 3- Purchase of 40,000 boxes of malaria rapid diagnostic tests, Pf/Pan antigens, HRP2/pLDH, 25 kit 4- Purchase of 4,000 boxes of rapid diagnostic tests (NS1 and IgM) for detection of severe dengue cases 5- Purchase of ELISA equipment for detection of dengue, chikungunya fever and West Nile virus 6- Purchase of RT-PCR kits (reagents) for arthropod-borne viral diseases. 7. Supporting the active case surveillance unit in pre-elimination areas in Hadhramaut. 8. Active surveillance of cases in Socotra in Hadhramaut/Socotra. 9. Purchasing 1,300,000 impregnated bednets sufficient for 2,600,000 people. 10. Purchasing residual insecticides. 11. Implementing various spraying campaigns. 12. Paying salaries to local and international experts from the World Health Organization.

The project is an extension of the first phase of the Malaria Control and Prevention Project in Yemen. The Gulf Cooperation Council countries funded the second phase with $12,000,000. The project includes a wide variety of preventive activities, including the distribution of 1,300,000 impregnated bednets and spraying campaigns targeting more than 500,000 homes with residual insecticides, in addition to other spraying campaigns with a variety of insecticides. The project also includes the purchase and provision of medications for adult patients, children, and pregnant women with malaria, as well as the provision of 1,000,000 rapid malaria detectors, in addition to medical supplies for laboratories and various types of investigation activities. It also supports the Yemeni National Program with the necessary equipment and devices to combat the epidemic.

The project will contribute to the diagnosis of several diseases, including: 1. Reducing the incidence and mortality rates resulting from severe malaria, including mosquito-borne diseases. 2. Reducing insecticide resistance in the vector. Detecting genetic mutations in the parasite and vector. 3. Building and developing the Yemeni malaria control and prevention program. 4. Contributing to making the Arabian Peninsula malaria-free.
